facts.text: The striated thornbill wears a russet- or orange-brown crown streaked with cream, and cream underparts heavily streaked with black.
facts.quote: It has a russet- or orange-brown crown with cream streaks, dull yellow-olive upperparts, olive-grey flanks, and cream underparts heavily streaked with black.

facts.text: The striated thornbill is a tiny bird, only 9–10 centimetres long and weighing around 7 grams.
facts.quote: The adult striated thornbill is 9–10 centimetres (3.5–3.9 in) long and weighs around 7 grams (0.25 oz).

facts.text: The striated thornbill feeds mostly on insects, gleaning them from leaves high in the canopy of eucalypt trees.
facts.quote: The striated thornbill is predominantly insectivorous, generally forages in the canopy of eucalypt trees, gleaning leaves for prey.

facts.text: It often hangs upside-down while foraging for food.
facts.quote: It often hangs upside-down while foraging.

facts.text: The striated thornbill feeds on nectaries on sunshine wattle leaves, helping pollinate the plant as it brushes against flower heads.
facts.quote: The striated thornbill also visits and feeds on extra-floral nectaries on the leaves of sunshine wattle (Acacia terminalis), helping pollinate the plant as it brushes against flower heads while feeding.

facts.text: Outside the breeding season, striated thornbills form flocks of 7–20 birds from late summer to winter.
facts.quote: Striated thornbills form flocks of 7–20 birds outside of breeding season from late summer to winter, before breaking up into groups of 2–4, composed of a breeding pair plus helper birds.

facts.text: When breeding time arrives, the flocks break into groups of 2–4 birds made up of a breeding pair plus helpers.
facts.quote: before breaking up into groups of 2–4, composed of a breeding pair plus helper birds.

facts.text: The striated thornbill is found only in Australia, where it lives in subtropical or tropical dry forests.
facts.quote: It is endemic to Australia, where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.

facts.text: A genetic study found the striated thornbill's ancestor diverged from that of the yellow thornbill around 6 million years ago.
facts.quote: A 2017 genetic study using both mitochondrial and nuclear DNA found that the ancestor of the striated thornbill diverged from that of the yellow thornbill around 6 million years ago.
